key_insight: Task-aware fusion of complementary structural encoders improves materials property prediction by selecting representations from property-relevant network depths.
engineering_relevance: A lightweight bridge connects structural encoders to a language model with fewer trainable parameters and half the overall training time reported for MatterChat.
method: Combine CHGNet features with intermediate Zatom-1 representations.
Use task-conditioned latent queries to select and fuse structural information through attention.
Train directly on downstream prediction tasks, jointly learning fusion and material-language alignment without separate contrastive pretraining.
evidence_signal: Across classification and regression tasks, TCAF outperforms MatterChat with up to 47.8% lower RMSE; adding UMA-S yields the highest reported macro-average classification accuracy of 89.61%.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify datasets or evaluation splits, limiting assessment of generalization to unseen materials.
paper_title: Choosing the Right Representations: Task-Aware Fusion for Multimodal Materials Language Models
